subject: Data classification and where LLM prompts/outputs are stored — post-demo commitments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stein <alex.stein@pinebridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Data classification and where LLM prompts/outputs are stored — post-demo commitments

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap + the specific commitments we discussed around PII handling for prompts/outputs so your legal and engineering teams have something concrete to review. Marked action items at the bottom.

Summary of what we showed
- Live demo used ephemeral sessions (no default persistence).
- We highlighted the Dedicated option (VPC) and Private deployment for customers that need on-prem or strict residency.

Redwood commitments (high level)
1) Prompt and model output default behavior
   - By default (hosted API): transient KV cache for active sessions only; we do not persist prompt or generated output to long-term object storage. KV cache is memory-backed and evicted after session termination (~minutes).
   - If you enable "debug retention" for a workspace, prompts + outputs are captured into an encrypted S3 bucket for debugging and retained for a configurable TTL (default 30 days). This setting is opt-in per-account and gated by an admin toggle.

2) Telemetry, logs, and sampling
   - Structured telemetry (request metadata: model, latency, token counts) is collected for observability. We sample full-text payloads for debugging at a configurable rate (0% by default for new accounts).
   - For customers on Dedicated/Private, telemetry routing can be configured to push logs to customer-managed sinks (CloudWatch / Stackdriver / S3).

3) PII detection and automatic redaction
   - We offer server-side field redaction rules (regex + named-entity classifiers). When enabled, detected PII (SSNs, credit card numbers, full MRNs) is masked in persisted captures and in telemetry exports.
   - Redaction is available as a pre-processing step and also as an optional post-processing rule applied before any retention.

4) Encryption & key control
   - At rest: persisted captures (when enabled) are encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated/Private; hosted accounts may use Redwood-managed keys unless enterprise KMS is requested.
   - In-transit: TLS for all endpoints; internal inter-service traffic is mTLS.

5) Residency options
   - Hosted API: choose region (us-east-1 or eu-west-1) at account creation; persisted captures follow the chosen region.
   - Dedicated/Private: can be deployed in customer VPC / on-premise for strict data locality.

6) Deletion and TTLs
   - Default: ephemeral session cache (minutes) + telemetry (90 days for aggregated metrics; raw sampled payloads only if debug retention enabled).
   - If debug retention enabled: retained payloads TTL configurable 7/30/90 days; we default to 30.

Attachments
- Attached: redwood-pii-matrix-v2.pdf (mapping of capture categories + recommended settings).

Next steps / asks (mutual action plan)
- Alex: confirm whether Pinebridge wants debug retention enabled for the initial PoC (yes/no) and which region you require.
- LegalOps: if you want explicit wording for the SOW re: retention TTLs, I can send a short addendum.
- Marissa: can you provision the trial Dedicated instance if they want VPC demo?

Thanks — I put the matrix attached; happy to walk through line-by-line.

--

Subject: Re: Data classification and where LLM prompts/outputs are stored — post-demo commitments

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few follow-ups from our security and legal teams: 

1) Clarify "KV cache" — is any part of the prompt or output written to disk on the host or to object storage as part of normal operation (not debug retention)? If so, what filesystem encryption + retention applies?

2) For hosted accounts, if we do not opt into debug retention, are you able to guarantee no customer prompt text will leave the region we select (e.g., us-east-1)? We need to ensure no cross-region fallback for model availability.

3) Can you confirm the redaction classifier accuracy metrics or provide an example false-positive/false-negative rate for common PHI categories? Legal is especially interested in how redaction might impact debugging.

4) Please include a short summary we can drop into our vendor questionnaire: "What is stored, where, for how long" for LLM prompts and outputs.

If you can send that summary + the answers to the four asks by Friday, we'll route to procurement. Also copying our Security engineer (Legal Ops is cc'd).

—Alex
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stein <alex.stein@pinebridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Legal Ops <legal@pinebridgehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data classification and where LLM prompts/outputs are stored — post-demo commitments

Alex — answering each ask inline and including the short vendor-friendly summary at the bottom.

1) KV cache behavior
   - Operationally the KV cache used for attention/key-value caching is in-memory on the inference host and is not persisted to long-term object storage during normal operation. Short-lived swap/eviction may touch local ephemeral disk in certain failure/scale scenarios; those disks are encrypted at rest and rotated. For Dedicated/Private we can ensure the cache stays in RAM-only if you require.

2) Cross-region guarantees
   - For hosted accounts we provide regional placement guarantees: account-level placement to a chosen region and the control plane respects that for inference routing; we do not route customer payloads cross-region unless you opt into multi-region failover. We can include a technical SOW clause prohibiting cross-region fallback for your PoC.

3) Redaction classifier performance
   - Our NER-based redaction model combined with deterministic regexes yields: precision ~0.98, recall ~0.92 on our internal healthcare test-set (examples: MRN, DOB, SSN). We provide exportable evaluation artifacts upon NDA. We recommend conservative configuration for persistence: enable pre-ingest regex masking for high-confidence tokens and use NER-based masking for softer matches.

4) Short vendor summary (copy/paste for questionnaire)
   - "What is stored": By default no long-term storage of raw prompts or generated outputs. Transient in-memory KV cache for active sessions; structured telemetry (model, token counts, latency) collected. Persisted captures only if the customer opts into 'debug retention' or uses Dedicated/Private with explicit retention.
   - "Where": Region-selected object storage (us-east-1 or eu-west-1) for persisted captures. Dedicated/Private: optional in-customer VPC or on-prem deployment under customer control.
   - "For how long": Default: ephemeral cache (minutes). Telemetry (aggregated metrics) 90 days. Persisted captures (if enabled): configurable TTL defaults to 30 days (options: 7/30/90).

Additional notes
- KMS: Hosted accounts use Redwood-managed KMS by default; enterprise customers can supply their own KMS keys for Dedicated/Private.
- Audit logs: admin-level audit trails (who toggled retention, who accessed captures) are retained 365 days for enterprise plans.

Attachments included: redwood-pii-matrix-v2.pdf, plus a blank mapping template (pinebridge-mapping-template.xlsx) to map your fields to our redaction rules.

If that looks ok I'll draft the SOW clause and Marissa will kick off the Dedicated test if you want VPC isolation.

Thanks —
Jordan
